query:
The notion that one might be justified in behaving irrationally in the service of a sufficiently worthy end is incoherent. For if such an action is justified, then one would be behaving rationally, not irrationally.

The argument that one cannot intend to spill a glass of water accidentally and that spilling it accidentally means that the act will not have been done intentionally is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above.
